name: Driftclean Pressed Occasion Suit (the Gray Zone Cut)
description:
A two-piece suit assembled from mismatched but color-matched salvage: jacket from one donor garment, trousers from another. The Driftclean Collective operates out of a Tier 1 basement laundry, doing alterations and suit-matching for people who need to look legitimate for legal proceedings, employment interviews, or family events. They've developed a practiced eye for pairing fabrics that read as a set under fluorescent light. The jacket is taken in with interior basting stitches that hold but won't survive aggressive movement. The trousers have a crease ironed so sharp it compensates for the slightly wrong shade of charcoal.

The Collective charges by the hour and by complexity. A basic match-and-press runs Φ8–Φ12. They keep a rack of assembled suits available for immediate loan or purchase. Regulars know to return the suit after the hearing — it goes back on the rack for the next person who needs it.
cultural_context: The Driftclean Collective is a known institution in its district. People give them donor garments voluntarily. There's no shame in wearing a Collective suit — it's understood as community infrastructure. A few Tier 2 labor organizers wear them deliberately as political statement.
story_hooks: The character borrows a Collective suit for a custody hearing. The jacket belonged to a man who died in a Crucible furnace accident — his name is written in faded marker on the interior lining. The character wins the hearing.
Someone is trying to shut down the Collective, citing 'unlicensed textile alteration' under a Corponation IP clause about donor garments. The Collective needs help.

A Vantablack analyst is running surveillance on a Tier 1 block and keeps seeing the same suit on different people at different legal events. It takes them three weeks to understand what they're looking at.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharply pressed two-piece suit that reads as unified formal wear at conversational distance, but reveals its assembled nature under close inspection. The jacket sits structured and tailored; the trousers hang with deliberate crease emphasis. Together they project legitimacy and professional intent—exactly calibrated for courtrooms, HR offices, and formal family settings.
physical_description.fit: Jacket is taken in through interior basting—snug through the shoulders and chest, with a slight restriction at the sides that demands careful movement. Trousers are straight-cut with a high, slightly tapered waist. The overall silhouette is conservative and intentional, with no excess fabric.
physical_description.primary_material: Salvaged suiting—likely a blend of recycled wool and synthetic fibers, composition varies slightly between jacket and trousers due to sourcing from different donor garments. Durable, mid-grade fabrics meant to survive multiple wearers.
physical_description.texture: Smooth and press-finished, with a subtle nap visible under raking light. The interior basting stitches are visible if you look, creating slight texture breaks in the jacket lining. The trouser crease is knife-sharp, almost aggressive—evidence of deliberate pressing technique.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matched charcoal with intentional variance: the jacket reads as a slightly warmer gray-brown under fluorescent light, while the trousers are cooler charcoal. Under natural light, the mismatch becomes apparent, but under the institutional lighting of courthouses and office buildings, they present as a cohesive suit. No patterns; solid tones only.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: two-button front closure with mother-of-pearl or polymer buttons, likely replaced to match the collected suit aesthetic. Trousers: standard flat front with zipper fly and single interior hook closure.
distinctive_features: Visible interior basting stitches holding the jacket seams—evidence of quick tailoring for durability over permanence
Aggressive trouser crease compensating for subtle fabric shade difference
Mixed-origin construction visible as slight fabric texture/finish variations between jacket and trousers under direct light
Hand-marked tailor chalk marks visible at interior seams if inspected closely
Wear pattern on the jacket left shoulder and hip pocket consistent with repeated wearing and return-to-rack handling
No identifying logos or brand markers; Driftclean's implicit signature is the quality of the match itself
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 accessibility, but Tier 2 street-cultural statement. The suit signals institutional legitimacy while its provenance (salvage, gray-market alteration) reads as deliberate class consciousness to those in the know.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing a Driftclean suit announces: 'I needed to be formal, I did it ethically and collectively, I understand institutional optics.' Common among labor organizers, legal aid recipients, people facing employment interviews or custody hearings. No shame—this is understood infrastructure. Tier 1 corpo who wear them are making a political choice; Tier 2 and 3 people wear them because the Collective has solved a real problem.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine in the moment of wearing (freshly pressed, basted seams intact), but showing micro-stress patterns from being worn then returned, pressed, and re-racked. The jacket shows light pilling on the shoulders and forearms from repeated wear. Trousers maintain their crease obsessively through the Collective's pressing protocols.
